Recommended for – Guitarists or bassists seeking sustain and definition with a tone full of personality. The White Russian is a faithful reproduction of the circuit of the Big Muff pedals produced by Sovtek in the early 90s. It is one of the versions of the circuit that has the most distinct sound, with more controlled bass and less gain than most of its Electro Harmonix siblings. These tighter bass frequencies make it one of the favorite pedals for bassists, maintaining definition even at higher gain levels. Its singing sustain captivates guitarists from various music genres, from David Gilmour (who used the Sovtek in the recording of Pulse) to Dan Auerbach, guitarist of the Black Keys. The White Russian celebrates the utilitarian look of the original Soviet Big Muff, but with various modern conveniences: reduced size, true bypass, metal film resistors – which drastically reduce the noise from the original design – and all the reliability of Collateral FX pedals. - **Archive parent:** P015 White Russian
- **Catalog identity:** P015 White Russian Distortion/Fuzz
- **Builder:** Collateral FX
- **Catalog type:** Fuzz / Distortion
- **Identity:** Collateral FX White Russian, a Sovtek Big Muff reproduction from the early 1990s family.

Collateral FX describes White Russian as a faithful reproduction of the Big Muff circuit used by Sovtek in the early 1990s. It targets the tighter bass and lower-gain character of the Russian version. [1]

The enclosure concept follows the utilitarian Soviet Big Muff visual language. No complete factory colorway sequence was established.

- Sovtek early-1990s Big Muff circuit target.
- True bypass.
- Reduced enclosure size.
- Metal-film resistors.
- 9V operation.
- Guitar and bass compatibility.
- 11 x 6 x 4 cm enclosure. [1]

The design is specifically tied to the early-1990s Sovtek/Russian version of the Big Muff circuit rather than a generic Big Muff.

Collateral FX identifies the circuit as a **silicon fuzz/distortion** design but does not publish exact transistor part numbers. [1]

No exact diode part number was published.

The manufacturer emphasizes controlled bass, somewhat lower gain, strong definition at high settings, and singing sustain, with guitar and bass compatibility. [1]
